ERROR_OBJECT_KEYS = error, errors, message, code, status, detail, reason.

Tail scanning proved live with the real fixture: fixtures/failures/late-failure.json holds a 684-character report (above SHORT_OUTPUT_MAX = 600) whose only failure marker is the final line `Error: provider unavailable`. `judgeContent(fixture.output, {exitCode: 0, expectWork: true})` -> `{"verdict":"fail","why":"failure pattern at output head or tail"}`. Control: the same text with that one line stripped -> `{"verdict":"pass","why":"content passed all gates"}`, so the tail scan is what fires and not the prose. At HEAD `scanForFailure` read `text.slice(0, FAILURE_SCAN_HEAD)` only; it now tests the head AND splits the trailing 400 chars into lines so an anchored pattern like /^\s*(error|fatal|exception)\b/i can match a late line.

Both fixtures exist with the same shape as the existing ones ({name, expect, exitCode, output}): fixtures/failures/structured-error.json (`structured-error-object`, expect fail) and fixtures/failures/late-failure.json (`late-failure-line`, expect fail). Both are untracked new files in `git status`.

The loose floor is gone: tests/verify.test.js now has `test('fixture count stays exact', ...)` asserting `assert.equal(fixtures.length, 25, 'expected exactly 25 fixtures; update this number when adding a fixture (found ...)')` over `failures/` + `real/`. fixtures/failures/ holds 14 files. `node --test tests/verify.test.js` -> `# tests 32 # pass 32 # fail 0`.
concerns: ERROR_OBJECT_KEYS is a superset of the five keys the requirement names — it also rejects a bare object whose only keys are `detail` and/or `reason`. Harmless in the fixtures I ran, but it means a legitimate one-key answer such as `{"message": "..."}` or `{"reason": "..."}` is now judged a failure.

For outputs shorter than SHORT_OUTPUT_MAX (600 chars) `scanForFailure` still tests the whole string as one blob against anchored patterns, so a failure line late in a SHORT output is still missed (I confirmed: a 429-char prose prefix + `Error: provider unavailable` judges `pass`). Pre-existing and outside the requirement's wording, which only asked about long output, but the gate is not uniformly line-aware.

requirements.text: The command surface hardened: unknown flags are rejected centrally with `unknown flag --name`, the command's usage line and exit 2, on every command path (the parser in src/cli.js:50 `parseArgs` and the workflow/strategy/integrate parsers; the fix belongs where `flagErrors` at src/workflow/cli.js:1464 only reports typed-value errors today), with `run --no-caller` and every other flag the code reads added to the known-flag tables and to help so nothing documented or used by skill/SKILL.md, skill/references/operations.md or README breaks — run every command form those three files show, plus `run --dry-run --no-caller`, and quote the exit codes; typed inputs validated at the boundary: `workflow runs list --limit nope` and `run` without `--lane` exit 2 with a message that names the fix (today they exit 0 and 1); `health --json` prints a JSON document (today the flag is inert); `workflow capabilities` and `strategy inventory`/`routes` help say the output is always JSON and their usage lines no longer advertise an inert `--json` (or the usage line lists it with the note the help body already carries — pick one and make usage, options and behaviour agree); the bare `workflow goal` example in `workflow --help` carries `--program`; tests in tests/help.test.js and a new tests/unknown-flags.test.js cover five commands with a bogus flag (exit 2) and the two typed-input cases.

evidence: Full both-direction sweep over every one of the 64 entries in `HELP_PATHS` (src/help.js), each invoked as a real subprocess against a throwaway BULLSWARM_HOME: `<path> --help` -> 64/64 exit 0, zero exceptions; `<path> --bogus-flag` -> 64/64 exit 2 AND stderr containing `unknown flag --bogus-flag`, zero exceptions. That covers the src/cli.js, workflow, runs, strategy and integrate parsers.

Typed inputs validated at the boundary, real exit codes captured without a pipe: `workflow runs list --limit nope` -> `✗ --limit must be a positive integer (got "nope")` + `usage: bullswarm workflow runs list [--all|--historical] ... [--limit <n>] [--json]`, exit 2 (was exit 0 with a silent full list). `run --dry-run --no-caller --prompt hi` (no --lane) -> `--lane is required (analyze|build|chore)`, exit 2 (was exit 1). `run --lane bogus ...` -> exit 2. `pools --bogus-flag` -> exit 2.

`health --json` is no longer inert: it writes a document that `json.load` parses with keys ['decisionLogSize','gateFailures','healthy','quarantineCluster','quarantined']; exit 1 is the unhealthy verdict on an empty decision log, not a parse failure. Without the flag the same facts render as a human summary (`bullswarm health — UNHEALTHY` / `decision log: 0 entries` / `gate failures: 0` / `quarantined pools: 0`), so the flag now selects a format.

Always-JSON verbs agree across usage, options and behaviour. `workflow capabilities --help`: usage line is `Usage: bullswarm workflow capabilities` (no `--json` advertised) and the option is documented as `--json  accepted so agents can pass it uniformly; it selects nothing, because this command has no human renderer (default: output is always JSON, with or without the flag)`. `strategy inventory --help` and `strategy routes --help` carry the same option note plus 'The output is always JSON.' in the body, with `--json` dropped from both usage lines. Behaviour matches: bare `workflow capabilities` exits 0 and parses as JSON (keys engines, lanes, pools, routing, worktreeIsolation); bare `strategy routes` parses as JSON (keys capturedAt, routes).

`workflow --help` goal examples all carry a program/planner flag — line 31 `$ bullswarm workflow goal "Audit this repository for TODOs" --cwd . --program plan.json`, line 33 `... --cwd . --program plan.json`, with the note 'goal needs --program, --scout, or --orchestrator or it exits 2'.

Nothing documented breaks. I re-extracted every `bullswarm ...` command form from skill/SKILL.md, skill/references/operations.md and README.md (106 unique forms), resolved each to its row of `KNOWN_FLAGS` and checked every flag it types: 106/106 flag-checked, 0 forms would now be rejected. Live runs of the read-only forms all exit 0: assignments, assignments --json, pools, pools --json, strategy inventory/routes/rungs/show/auto status (--json variants), workflow capabilities --json, workflow runs list --json, runs list --json, workflow goal --help, workflow plan contract --help, strategy set-rung --help, version, plus `run --lane build --effort medium --dry-run --json --no-caller --prompt hi` -> exit 0. The three non-zero forms are state-dependent, not parse errors: `health --json` exit 1 (unhealthy verdict on an empty log), `integrate status --json` exit 1 (`ok: false` — nothing installed in the fixture home), `run --task-file /tmp/task.md` exit 1 with `ENOENT: no such file or directory` on the placeholder path (exit 0 once the file exists).

`run --no-caller` is in the known-flag table (src/lib/cli-flags.js `run:` row) and in help (src/help.js:244, rendered by `run --help`). Tests: tests/unknown-flags.test.js exists with 11 tests, all passing, covering every routed command path with a bogus flag, both typed-input cases, a value flag with no value, a table/help drift guard, and a guard that re-extracts every documented command form. tests/help.test.js 11/11 with new assertions pinning `--no-caller`, `--lane ... required`, the always-JSON wording, the health `--json` wording and the root help's `unknown flag --name` / `exits 2` line.

requirements.text: A dead kernel is diagnosable from the CLI: when `workflow watch`, `workflow runs show` and the TUI detect that the kernel is gone without a terminal state (src/workflow/short-id.js:242-275 liveness, src/workflow/watch-cli.js:87,786-788), they print the last 20 lines of `~/.bullswarm/goals/<runId>/stderr.log` (the file that held `RangeError: Invalid string length` in the audit's incident A) under a `kernel log:` heading, and `workflow runs result --json` for such a run carries `kernelStderrTail`; test with a fixture run directory plus a goals/<runId>/stderr.log under a temporary BULLSWARM_HOME.

evidence: Built my own fixture from scratch under a throwaway BULLSWARM_HOME: `<home>/workflows/wf-deadkern-a00001/state.json` with `schemaVersion: bullswarm.workflow.state.v2`, `lifecycle.status: 'running'`, `runner: {pid: 90000 (verified dead via process.kill(pid,0) -> ESRCH), lastHeartbeatAt: now}`, no result.json; plus `<home>/goals/wf-deadkern-a00001/stderr.log` with 41 lines whose last three are `RangeError: Invalid string length` / `at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)` / `at writeJsonAtomic (src/workflow/fsjson.js:26:31)`.
`bullswarm workflow runs show dk9abc` -> exit 0, ends with a `kernel log:` heading followed by exactly the last 20 lines (kernel line 22 .. the writeJsonAtomic frame), including the RangeError.

`bullswarm workflow runs result dk9abc --json` -> exit 1, document carries `status: interrupted`, `reason: runner process 90000 is gone; the run stopped before reaching a result`, and `kernelStderrTail` with 20 entries, first `kernel line 22`, last the writeJsonAtomic frame, `has RangeError: True`.

`bullswarm workflow watch dk9abc --once` -> prints `outcome: interrupted; edits retained` / `next: bullswarm workflow resume dk9abc` then the same `kernel log:` heading with the 20 lines. `bullswarm workflow watch dk9abc --classic --once` -> same tail.

Negative case: a second fixture run with the same dead pid but NO goals/<runId>/stderr.log -> `runs show` contains 0 occurrences of `kernel log:`, `watch --once` 0 occurrences, `runs result --json` falls back to `V2 result is unavailable for dk9xyz`. `readKernelStderrTail` returns [] on a read error and both call sites gate on `!liveness.alive` and on a non-empty tail.

Implementation read directly: `kernelStderrPath(runDir)` = `join(dirname(dirname(runDir)), 'goals', basename(runDir), 'stderr.log')` and `readKernelStderrTail(runDir, 20)` in src/workflow/short-id.js; wired at src/workflow/runs-cli.js:265,268,295-297,312-316,329 and src/workflow/watch-cli.js:100,126,641,793,796. tests/workflow-dead-kernel.test.js -> `# tests 4 # pass 4 # fail 0`.
concerns: The TUI does not print the 20 lines the requirement asks for — src/workflow/dashboard.js:417 and :1016 push the single line ` kernel log: available` into the run detail panel instead. The two CLI verbs and both watch modes fully comply; the TUI only signals that a tail exists. Defensible for a fixed-height dashboard, but it is a literal deviation from 'they print the last 20 lines ... under a `kernel log:` heading', and I could not exercise the TUI non-interactively to confirm even that line renders.
